quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop. Stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying, what should you do?

options.text: Drive normally. Your emotions will not affect your driving.
Drive faster because you are more alert.
Calm down and focus before you start driving.
Call a friend while you drive to feel better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can distract you from driving. They take your mind off the road. Always take time to calm down and clear your mind before you start the engine.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as you.
Only if the pedestrian signals you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street. This is true even if the pedestrian crosses against the light or is being careless.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing with no traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: The driver must yield to pedestrians at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If the right lane is full, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear to let them pass.

questions.explanation: If tailgated, move right if possible. If not, slow down gradually when safe to let them pass. Never stop suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: What must you do when you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights. Drive immediately to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, pass through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low ground railroad crossing. Railroad tracks cross the road at a steep angle. The bottom of low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their high beams. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the oncoming vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight ahead down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the bright lights and helps you stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What do round signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you of an upcoming railroad crossing. Drive with extra caution when you see this sign.

questions.question: When may you NOT cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is broken down.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes only if it is safe and does not interfere with traffic.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic.
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only when driving in rural areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block traffic flow. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You feel calmer and can focus better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You feel calmer and can focus better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, changes how you judge speed and distance, makes it harder to recover from headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when they might not see you. For example, sound your horn if you think another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on an interstate?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you get tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing on an interstate. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Avoid changing lanes often. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving drunk. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: What does this sign show?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and see a heavy truck ahead. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.

questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Be careful when approaching from behind. When you cannot see clearly ahead on a hill, passing is not allowed.

questions.question: You reach a railroad crossing with flashing warning lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with warning signals, you must stop at least 15 feet from the track. Watch for a lowered gate or an approaching train.

questions.question: After a school bus stops to let children out, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After a school bus stops with its red lights flashing and stop arm out, watch for children walking along the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, which one has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right.
The vehicle coming from the left.
The vehicle whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without traffic signals, you must yield to vehicles coming from your right.

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no other vehicles are in the lane. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: An eight-sided sign is always a:
questions.explanation: All eight-sided signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop at every red octagonal sign.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is ahead. The road splits into two one-way roadways with a median or divider between them. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has a series of turns and curves.

questions.question: Taking drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Increases the risk of a crash.
Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Reduces the effects of alcohol on driving.
Does not affect your ability to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter) can affect your brain and impair your driving. Mixing alcohol with other drugs greatly increases your risk of crashing.

questions.question: Compared to daytime driving, night driving is:
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see in the dark, headlights can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers may be on the road.

questions.question: When driving on icy or snowy roads, what technique helps prevent crashes?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better traction.
Leave the highway as soon as possible.
Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on snow or ice. Slowing down and increasing your following distance are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign:

options.text: Warns you about conditions on or near the road.
Directs you to cities and towns ahead.
Tells you about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns you about conditions on or near the road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text or symbols on a yellow background. They alert you to conditions ahead on or near the road.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass another vehicle if the lane ahead is clear.

questions.question: If two drivers reach an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: If you reach an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, let that vehicle go first. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: A shared center lane on a two-way road is used for:
questions.explanation: Shared center lanes on two-way roads are for left turns and U-turns where permitted. Vehicles from both directions can use these lanes.
